text:
Aisha Rao: Heads up — saw an odd KV reuse pattern in prod that looks like prefix dedupe races + longctx memory growth. Paging spiked during a 10k token session workload. :eyes:

Tom Nguyen: Can you paste the top-line metrics? did resident set size grow or was it evictions?

Aisha Rao: RSS climbed ~1.2GB over ~40s for a single session, then we started seeing 5-10% more page faults overall. Eviction count jumped right after. Logs: `kv.resident=3.8GB -> 5.0GB`, `kv.evictions=412 -> 1302` in that interval.

Priya Patel: Hmm. Are keys being de-duplicated across sessions? we changed key format last month to include tenant_salt. Maybe mismatch there.

Aisha Rao: That's the thing — some requests still used the old key format when the runtime switched rollouts. So duplicates were coexisting: old-key and new-key for same prefix. Leads to fragmentation in the KV page table.

Santiago Lopez: Fragmentation would explain higher page scan times. Did you repro with synthetic load?

Aisha Rao: Yes — small repro harness: 200 concurrent sessions, half pinned to longctx (>8k tokens) and we flip key-format mid-run. Repro steps below:

```
# repro outline
start harness --sessions 200 --longctx 50%
wait 30s
rollout-config key_format=tenant_salt_v2
observe kv.metrics
```

Observed: resident growth + eviction storms when both key formats present.

Tom Nguyen: Could also be a race where cache entries are pinned per-session (session affinity) and the dedupe path doesn't merge entries when key formats change. That would double footprint.

Priya Patel: We should consider a migration-compatible canonicalizer: on read, map legacy keys to canonical fingerprint and collapse into one entry (best-effort). But careful — could cause invalidation semantics to change.

perf-bot: Alert: kv.page_fault_rate +120% over baseline for service/runtime-serve-1 during 1718005067-1718005200.

Santiago Lopez: Another angle: longctx grows KV value sizes (bigger KV chunks) which increases fragmentation inside pages. If we create a compacting GC for large sessions (merge contiguous small entries), we might reduce page churn.

Aisha Rao: Agree. Plan proposal: (1) immediate mitigation = pin rollout so we don't have mixed key formats in the same pool, (2) short-term patch = best-effort canonicalizer on read with TTL-preserving merge, (3) medium-term = small local compaction pass for large-session pages + add metrics for key-format-variants per-tenant.

Tom Nguyen: For (2) can you sketch the canonicalizer logic? we need pseudo-code for reviews.

Aisha Rao: Sketch:
```
function fetch(k):
  v = kv.get(k)
  if v: return v
  if looks_like_legacy(k):
    k2 = canonicalize(k)
    v2 = kv.get(k2)
    if v2:
      kv.set(k, v2, ttl_of(v2))  # best-effort attach
      return v2
  return null
```

Priya Patel: That will reduce duplicate residency over time as legacy keys touch canonical ones. We should guard with a per-tenant rate limit to avoid thundering updates.

Santiago Lopez: Also add a metric: kv.duplicates_by_key_format which counts coexisting legacy+new entries for same canonical fingerprint. That will help validate.

Aisha Rao: I'll open a quick RFC + small PR for the canonicalizer and the metric. For now I'm rolling back the config flip to stop mixed formats.

Tom Nguyen: Thanks — if you want I'll help run the compaction experiment on a staging shard.

Aisha Rao: Yes please. @Tom ping me and I'll share the harness + traces. :thumbsup:
